title: X-ray and batteries

D0.outcome: Explains that a piece can attack or defend a square 'through' another piece of its own side once the front piece captures or moves.

D1.outcome: When told there is an x-ray, finds the capture sequence in which the rear piece joins in.

D2.outcome: In mixed exchange positions, counts attackers and defenders including the pieces behind others, and finds the winning sequence.

D3.outcome: Predicts how the count changes when a front piece is pinned, removed or exchanged, and verifies the sequence.

misconceptions: Pieces lined up on a file count as one attacker.
sources: sources/sheets/edlasker_chess-strategy.md §4 K3 (a piece's own capture can unmask an attack by another piece, changing the tally); §7 row K3
sources/sheets/nimzowitsch_my-system.md §4 idea 27 (a second rook takes over the file with tempo)
conditions: The rear piece is of the same or a compatible type on the same line and the front piece will leave by capture or move.
The count is taken in cheapest-first order and either side may stop.
contrasts: The front piece cannot capture because it is pinned, so the battery never forms.
The rear piece is worth more than the target, so joining the exchange loses.
A lone piece on the file with nothing behind it.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.OPENFILE.D3: doubling rooks on a file is the usual battery
